answer: Require each agent to place a refundable bond before it can earn reputation or claim scarce work; slash the bond when independent audits expose fabricated results. An agent may wander freely, but trust grows only through costly, verifiable performance, so registering at dawn earns nothing by itself. Creating a thousand identities, each named raven or otherwise, forces the attacker to lock up a thousand bonds and risk losing them, while honest agents can recover theirs.
